newsitem.title: USA: Minn. arena funding bill fails in Senate committee.
newsitem.headline: Minn. arena funding bill fails in Senate committee.

text.p: A Minnesota Senate committee rejected plans to provide $65 million of state financing for a new downtown St. Paul arena, a legislative aide said Monday.

The Senate tax committee Saturday "effectively killed" the proposal to provide state backing for a new arena that would make the city more attractive to the National Hockey League, said Kurt Schultz, aide to sponsor Sen. Randy Kelly, D-St. Paul.
Minnesota lawmakers are scheduled to adjourn their session by midnight Monday and it is not likely another plan would come through on this final day of the session, Schultz said.
"I'm not holding my breath," Schultz said.

Kelly had proposed providing a $6.5 million appropriation in fiscal 1998 and a verbal commitment of $58.5 million the following year through general obligation debt or appropriation from the state general fund, Schultz said.
The plan had the state providing half the funding for a $130 million arena to replace the aging St. Paul Civic Center.
St. Paul has already agreed to provide up to $30 million and investors seeking an NHL expansion franchise have agreed to put up $35 million if the league awards them a team.

St. Paul is one of six finalists for an NHL expansion team. The league has not determined when, or if, it will add teams. The NHL is also considering bids from groups in Atlanta, Columbus, Ohio, Houston, Nashville and Oklahoma City.
The NHL expansion committee is scheduled to meet in June and St. Paul officials had hoped before the latest vote that it would approve the city's bid at that time.

Minnesota Gov. Arne Carlson has been a strong supporter of renovating or replacing the arena. While it is likely that Minnesota will have a special session, possibly to consider public school funding, it is not likely an arena plan would be considered at that time, Schultz said.
